# Errors

> This page is generated from the same OpenAPI document the product is built from. If it disagrees with the product, the product wins - then tell us.

Every non-2xx response from the control API has the same body, and the ingest endpoint on the data plane uses the same envelope and the same codes (see [Ingest](./01-ingest.md) for the codes it emits). Branch on `error.code`, never on `error.message`; quote `error.request_id` when you ask for help.

## The envelope

The response body of EVERY non-2xx response from this API. There is no other error shape: every failure, including an unhandled internal error, is rendered as this envelope - the latter with `code: "internal_error"`.

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid_request",
    "message": "string",
    "request_id": "req_2f8b0c1e-6a4d-4c2e-9f10-3b5a7c9d1e22"
  }
}
```

| Property | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `error` | object | yes |  |  |
| `error.code` | string | yes | one of `invalid_request`, `unauthenticated`, `forbidden`, `email_not_verified`, `not_found`, `conflict`, `limit_exceeded`, `idempotency_key_reused`, `payload_too_large`, `rate_limited`, `internal_error` | STABLE and machine-readable - branch on this, never on `message`. Codes are never removed or repurposed, only added. Several share an HTTP status on purpose: `conflict`, `limit_exceeded` and `idempotency_key_reused` are all 409, and a client that must tell them apart was previously reduced to matching on the human-readable sentence. |
| `error.message` | string \| string[] | yes |  | For a HUMAN. A STRING on most errors, but a STRING ARRAY on a validation failure, with one entry per rejected field - and that array is the only per-field breakdown this API returns. Narrow before rendering it. |
| `error.request_id` | string | yes |  | The correlation id, echoed from a well-formed `x-request-id` or minted here. It appears on the matching log lines; quote it in a bug report. |
| `error.details` | object | no |  | Structured, code-specific context. ABSENT on most errors. Two shapes are part of the contract: `limit_exceeded` ALWAYS carries `{ limit, current, resource }` - the ceiling, what the tenant holds now, and which resource - and `rate_limited` carries `retry_after_seconds`. The message is for a human; these are the contract. Other codes may add keys, so this is not closed. |

## Codes

The status column is the HTTP status the code is returned with, as documented on the operations that name it. "Operations" counts the control-API operations whose responses list the code; the ingest endpoint is not in this document and is not counted. Two things the per-operation lists do not repeat: every operation that takes a body or query parameters can answer `400 invalid_request` when validation fails, and every operation can answer `500 internal_error`.

| Code | Status | Operations |
|---|---|---|
| [`invalid_request`](#invalid-request) | 400 Bad Request | 8 |
| [`unauthenticated`](#unauthenticated) | 401 Unauthorized | 0 |
| [`forbidden`](#forbidden) | 403 Forbidden | 66 |
| [`email_not_verified`](#email-not-verified) | 403 Forbidden | 66 |
| [`not_found`](#not-found) | 404 Not Found | 64 |
| [`conflict`](#conflict) | 409 Conflict | 25 |
| [`limit_exceeded`](#limit-exceeded) | 409 Conflict | 25 |
| [`idempotency_key_reused`](#idempotency-key-reused) | 409 Conflict | 25 |
| [`payload_too_large`](#payload-too-large) | 413 Payload Too Large | 0 |
| [`rate_limited`](#rate-limited) | 429 Too Many Requests | 15 |
| [`internal_error`](#internal-error) | 500 Internal Server Error | 0 |

### invalid_request

HTTP 400 Bad Request.

The request was malformed or failed validation: a missing or unknown field, a value outside its constraints, a bad query parameter, a body that is not JSON. Any operation that takes a body or query parameters can return it, whether or not it lists a 400 below; on a validation failure `error.message` is an array with one entry per rejected field.

### unauthenticated

HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

No credential, or one that is no longer valid: a missing, expired or revoked session cookie; at the ingest endpoint, a missing, malformed, unknown, revoked or expired API key. The message is deliberately the same for every cause.

### forbidden

HTTP 403 Forbidden.

You are authenticated and inside this tenant, but your role does not grant the permission the operation needs; `error.details.required_permissions` and `error.details.role` say which. Also returned for anything but a read while the organization or project is suspended, and at the ingest endpoint for a key whose project is not active or whose environment does not match.

### email_not_verified

HTTP 403 Forbidden.

The password was correct, but the address on the account has never been confirmed. Distinct from `unauthenticated` so a client can offer to resend the verification link.

### not_found

HTTP 404 Not Found.

The resource does not exist, or it belongs to another tenant. The two are one answer with one message on purpose, so an id scraped from elsewhere cannot be confirmed as live.

### conflict

HTTP 409 Conflict.

The request is well-formed but the current state refuses it: a duplicate name or slug, an endpoint that is deleted or has no live signing secret, a concurrent writer, an idempotency key whose first request is still in flight. Read the message, then act; match on the code.

### limit_exceeded

HTTP 409 Conflict.

A per-tenant resource ceiling was reached (projects per organization; keys, endpoints or subscriptions per project; deliveries per replay). Retry after freeing a slot. `error.details` always carries `{ limit, current, resource }`.

`error.details` carries:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | number | The ceiling that was reached. Always present on `limit_exceeded`. |
| `current` | number | What the tenant holds now. Always present on `limit_exceeded`. |
| `resource` | string | Which resource the ceiling covers. Always present on `limit_exceeded`. |

### idempotency_key_reused

HTTP 409 Conflict.

The `Idempotency-Key` was already used, within its window, with a different request body. The first request stands; this one created nothing. Use a new key for a new operation.

### payload_too_large

HTTP 413 Payload Too Large.

The request body exceeds the maximum event size the deployment allows. The message states the limit in bytes.

### rate_limited

HTTP 429 Too Many Requests.

Too many requests in the window. Wait for `Retry-After` seconds (also in `error.details.retry_after_seconds`) and try again; retrying sooner is what the limit exists to stop.

`error.details` carries:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `retry_after_seconds` | number | How long to wait before retrying. Present on `rate_limited`; mirrors the `Retry-After` header. |

### internal_error

HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.

Something failed on our side and nothing was changed that you can see. Retry with backoff; if it persists, quote `error.request_id` when you report it.
